To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Arp1 protein is capable of polymerizing into short filaments, but not long filaments, and that the length of Arp filaments is determined by a ruler mechanism.

1) Arp1 polymerizes into short filaments in vitro; 2) these polymers are capped at both ends by Arp1; and 3) the Arp1 filaments do not anneal into long filaments, even after prolonged incubation at high concentrations of Arp1 and ATP.

1) Arp1 is a highly conserved actin-like protein; 2) Arp1 assembles into filaments in vitro that are similar, but not the same, in length to the Arp1 filaments of dynactin; and 3) the Arp1 polymer is self-regulated and never attains the length of conventional filaments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the actin related protein (Arp) family.
understanding the mechanism of actin-related protein (Arp) polymerization.
the self-regulation of the polymerization of Arp1, a protein that plays a central role in the dynein motor complex and the mitotic spindle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arp1 is a novel actin homolog with a unique polymerization mechanism that generates short filaments with a uniform length.
Arp1 self-assembles into filaments in vitro, and the length of these filaments may be regulated in a novel way.
the Arp1 filaments are self-regulated, and the length of the filaments is regulated by the Arp1 molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Arp1 is capable of self-regulated polymerization into filaments that are similar, but not the same as, those found in dynactin and conventional actin.
Arp1 is able to polymerize in a manner distinct from that of conventional actin.
Arp1 polymerizes into a filament that has a length that is determined by a ruler activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-assembly of Arp1 can be regulated in vitro.
the Arp1 polymerization mechanism is fundamentally different from that of conventional actin.
, like conventional actin, Arp1 polymerization is regulated by the presence of a capping protein.
